raw_response:
I've been working this land for over 30 years. My father farmed before me, and his father before that. I know this soil. I know what Quzhou weather does to crops. I don't need a government booklet to tell me what to plant — I've learned by doing, by watching neighbors, by losing harvests I shouldn't have lost when I was young.

My 5 mu runs wheat in winter, maize in summer. Same land, both seasons. That's how we do it here and how we've always done it. My wife and two of my kids work in the city now, so I manage this mostly alone with my wife's help during busy periods. The farm isn't our only income, but it feeds the family and I won't let it go to waste.

**Wheat:** I'll plant around mid-October. I buy my seed from the village supply station — they sell Jimai varieties, improved lines that the county recommends. I don't use old saved seed anymore, learned that lesson 15 years ago when yields dropped. I'll apply compound fertilizer (diammonium phosphate) at sowing, then topdress with urea at green-up in spring. I water at sowing if the soil is dry, then again at jointing and heading — 3 irrigations total from my well. I'll spray herbicide in early spring, and watch for aphids before heading. Rotary till after maize harvest to prepare the seedbed.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in June, I'll rotary till quickly and get maize in fast — can't waste days. I use Xianyu 335 or whatever hybrid the seed shop has this year that my neighbors are buying. Same compound fertilizer at planting, urea topdressing when the plant is knee-high. Summer rains help so I'll only irrigate once or twice if it gets dry. Spray herbicide right after planting. Maybe one more spray if I see corn borer signs.

I won't try anything new this year. I have 7 mouths to think about.
